issues.legal_issue: A claim of title does not establish a right to defend property when the opposing party's possession is proved and the claimant's possession is not.
material_facts: The prosecution evidence, accepted by both lower courts, showed that the deceased owner had possessed and used the disputed grove.
The accused relied on documents relevant to title, but those documents did not establish their possession.
The Supreme Court was prepared to assume, for purposes of argument, that the land belonged to the accused, but the concurrent finding about possession remained unrebutted.
issues.conclusion: The accused had no established right of defence of the property, and their claim of title did not displace the finding that the deceased owner was in possession.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished title from possession in assessing a claim of defence of property. It relied on the concurrent factual finding of possession; it cited no earlier case or specific statutory provision for this conclusion.

rule.if: appeal_against_conviction and opposing_party_possession_proved and accused_possession_not_proved and title_evidence_does_not_establish_possession

predicates.appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal against a criminal conviction in which a right to defend property is claimed.
predicates.opposing_party_possession_proved: Evidence accepted by the courts shows that the opposing party possessed and used the disputed property.
predicates.accused_possession_not_proved: The accused do not establish that they possessed the disputed property.
predicates.title_evidence_does_not_establish_posses: The evidence relied on to show title does not establish possession of the disputed property.

issues.definition: When an appeal against conviction involves a property-defence claim, the defence is unavailable if the opposing party's possession is proved, the accused's possession is not proved, and their title evidence does not establish possession.

issues.legal_issue: A claim of defence of person fails when the circumstances do not reasonably indicate an imminent danger to the accused.
material_facts: The accused arrived armed with firearms, while the prosecution evidence indicated that the opposing group was unarmed.
The opposing group was attempting to resolve the land dispute through intermediaries, and some of its members were leaving when shots were fired.

Shots were fired at close range in some instances, but the evidence did not establish that the groups were all at such close quarters as to create a reasonable belief that the accused's lives were in danger.
The accused's injuries were simple and not incised, and shots were fired and people chased even as the opposing group fled.
issues.conclusion: The circumstances did not give the accused reasonable cause to fire in defence of their persons.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed whether the circumstances gave the accused a reasonable apprehension of danger warranting defence of person. It cited no earlier case or specific statutory provision for this conclusion.

rule.if: appeal_against_conviction and accused_armed and opposing_group_fleeing_when_shots_fired and no_reasonable_apprehension_of_imminent_danger

predicates.appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal against a criminal conviction in which defence of person is claimed.
predicates.accused_armed: The accused entered the incident armed with weapons.
predicates.opposing_group_fleeing_when_shots_fired: Members of the opposing group were fleeing when shots were fired at them.
predicates.no_reasonable_apprehension_of_imminent_d: The circumstances do not reasonably indicate that the accused faced imminent danger to their persons.

issues.definition: In an appeal against conviction, personal defence is unavailable where the accused were armed, the opposing group was fleeing when shots were fired, and the circumstances did not indicate imminent danger to the accused.

issues.legal_issue: Irregularities in a criminal investigation do not by themselves justify an adverse inference or undermine the prosecution when they are not shown to be dishonest or to have prejudiced the accused.
material_facts: The investigation included an unreliable account of when a witness's statement was recorded, a missing case-diary page, disputes about the time the investigation began, and the non-production of one of two allegedly recovered sticks.
The Court considered the investigation not above board and accepted that there had been defects and irregularities.
The lower courts found that the irregularities had not been shown to cause prejudice or to result from deliberate dishonesty or an improper motive.
The Court found the other evidence and circumstances sufficiently clear to sustain the findings.
issues.conclusion: The irregularities did not warrant an adverse inference against the prosecution or undermine the convictions because prejudice and deliberate dishonest conduct were not established.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle that mere defects or irregularities in investigation are insufficient to undermine proceedings unless the investigating officer abused the position, acted dishonestly or with an oblique motive, or the accused suffered prejudice. It rejected the contention that prejudice follows automatically. No earlier case was cited; Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was mentioned in connection with the disputed witness statement.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_challenging_conviction and investigation_irregularities and no_proven_prejudice and no_proven_deliberate_dishonesty and prosecution_evidence_remains_clear

predicates.criminal_appeal_challenging_conviction: The proceeding is a criminal appeal in which the accused challenge convictions by relying on defects in the investigation.
predicates.investigation_irregularities: The investigation contains procedural defects or inconsistencies in its records or conduct.
predicates.no_proven_prejudice: The accused have not shown that the investigation defects prejudiced their case.
predicates.no_proven_deliberate_dishonesty: The evidence does not establish that the investigating officers acted deliberately and dishonestly or with an improper motive.
predicates.prosecution_evidence_remains_clear: The remaining evidence and circumstances clearly support the prosecution findings.

issues.definition: Investigation irregularities do not undermine a conviction when, in a criminal appeal, the accused show no prejudice or deliberate dishonest conduct and the remaining prosecution evidence remains clear.

issues.legal_issue: Concurrent findings that an accused was present and participated in an offence should not be disturbed when witness identification is corroborated and no strong ground for interference is shown.
material_facts: Several eyewitnesses identified the accused as present with the armed group, and some also identified him in a jail identification procedure.
The accused's firearm was his, and a ballistic examination detected combustion products in its barrel washing.
The accused was absent from his workplace around the time of the incident and did not provide evidence that he was elsewhere.
The accused's name was not specified in some contemporaneous accounts, but those accounts referred to several members of the same group without naming them individually.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the concurrent finding that the accused was present and participated, finding no strong ground to interfere.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the corroboration of eyewitness identification and the absence of a strong ground to disturb concurrent factual findings. It cited no earlier case or specific statutory provision.

rule.if: appeal_against_conviction and concurrent_presence_findings and eyewitness_identification and corroborating_circumstances and no_strong_ground_to_interfere

predicates.appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal against a criminal conviction based in part on the accused's presence at the offence.
predicates.concurrent_presence_findings: The trial court and appellate court both found that the accused was present and participated.
predicates.eyewitness_identification: Witnesses identified the accused as present with the group involved in the incident.
predicates.corroborating_circumstances: Independent evidence or circumstances support the eyewitness identification.
predicates.no_strong_ground_to_interfere: The appellant has not shown a strong reason to disturb the concurrent factual findings.

issues.definition: A concurrent finding of presence is upheld in a conviction appeal when eyewitness identification is corroborated and no strong ground for interference is shown.

issues.legal_issue: A sentence enhancement cannot be sustained on a distinction between accused persons when the stated basis for the distinction applies equally to others convicted of comparable conduct.
material_facts: The trial court imposed life imprisonment on the accused convicted of the relevant killings, treating their drunkenness as an extenuating circumstance.
The High Court enhanced the sentences of two accused to death because the prosecution had directly connected them with the deaths of more than one person.

The Supreme Court observed that other accused must also have been responsible for causing the deaths of some of the deceased, so the stated reason did not distinguish the two enhanced sentences from the others.
The High Court did not enhance the sentences of those other accused on the same stated basis.
issues.conclusion: The Court set aside the High Court's enhancement and restored the sentences imposed by the trial court; it also considered the trial court's reliance on drunkenness as an extenuating circumstance unsound.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the stated ground for enhancement was unsound where it applied equally to accused whose sentences were not enhanced. It also rejected drunkenness, on the facts described, as a sound reason for imposing a lesser sentence. No earlier case or specific statutory provision was cited for the sentencing conclusion.

predicates.appeal_from_sentence_enhancement: The proceeding challenges an appellate court's decision to enhance a criminal sentence.
predicates.enhancement_based_on_multiple_deaths: The sentence was enhanced because the accused were connected with the deaths of more than one person.
predicates.same_basis_applies_to_unenhanced_coaccus: The stated reason for enhancement applies equally to co-accused whose sentences were not enhanced.

issues.definition: An enhancement is set aside when the stated basis for enhancing a sentence applies equally to co-accused whose sentences were left unchanged.
